reply.title: Why does a sigmoid squash any number into 0 to 1?
reply.story: When building models that make binary choices, we often need to turn any real number into a probability between zero and one. If we just use a linear function, the output grows without bound and breaks our rules. We need a smooth, S-shaped curve that maps infinite inputs into a strict finite range. Pierre François Verhulst faced this exact problem when studying population growth and introduced the logistic function. As the input grows very large or very negative, the exponential term dominates and bounds the output strictly between zero and one.
reply.cardDescription: Explore how the logistic sigmoid maps infinite inputs into a finite $0$ to $1$ range. Adjust steepness and midpoint to see the S-curve change.
reply.instructions: Adjust the steepness and midpoint sliders to reshape the sigmoid curve and observe the output and slope at the marker.
